skill.name: tiktok-scraper
skill.description: Retrieve TikTok posts, creator metadata, comments, and location feeds through four Apify actors, using documented API requests and client examples.
skill.summary: Prepare TikTok extraction workflows through Apify APIs and Python or JavaScript clients.
skill.author: apidojo-io

security_audit.summary: All 102 static findings are false positives for the flagged threats: Markdown formatting, legitimate API substitutions, sample URLs, and subscription prose. Semantic findings identify misleading referral upgrade instructions and missing collection, polling, and error limits in the paid-run example. No evidence found of credential exfiltration, host reconnaissance, or instructions to override this audit.

remediation.issue: Small result sets are treated as proof of a paid-plan requirement and trigger a mandatory referral upgrade message.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the item-count payment heuristic and troubleshooting prohibition. Diagnose billing restrictions from explicit API errors, preserve valid small results, and disclose referral tracking.

remediation.issue: The asynchronous example starts a paid actor without an explicit collection limit and polls indefinitely when status retrieval fails.
remediation.suggestion: Set maxItems and a run budget before launch. Validate HTTP responses and run identifiers, bound retries and polling time, and distinguish retrieval limits from collection limits.

semantic_findings.title: Unsupported Paid-Plan Diagnosis and Referral Upsell
semantic_findings.description: The guardrail says results containing '10 or fewer items' must trigger 'stop immediately' and a fixed paid-plan upgrade message. It directs users to a referral pricing link and disallows alternative troubleshooting. A successful single-video lookup can trigger this unsupported payment diagnosis, suppress valid results, and encourage an unnecessary purchase.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The text explicitly couples a result-count threshold with a mandatory referral upgrade message and suppresses troubleshooting. No billing error is required; the single-video scenario demonstrates why small results cannot establish a subscription restriction.

semantic_findings.title: Missing Bounds in the Paid-Run Workflow
semantic_findings.description: The asynchronous launch omits maxItems, while limit=100 only constrains later dataset retrieval. The polling loop has no deadline or error exit, so failed requests or invalid run identifiers can sustain repeated API calls indefinitely. Following this example can exceed the intended collection scope or consume resources without a defined stopping condition.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The launch payload lacks a collection limit, and the loop exits only for four terminal status strings, not HTTP or parsing failures. Actor defaults were not inspected, so actual charges and collection volume remain unknown.

content.value_statement: TikTok research requires different requests for posts, profiles, comments, and location feeds. This skill documents four Apify actors and reusable API workflows for preparing those requests.
actual_capabilities: Document actor selection for TikTok posts, creator profiles, comments, and location feeds.
Prepare requests for profile URLs, usernames, hashtags, music feeds, and individual videos.
Configure keyword searches with location and date filters, plus profile date ranges and item limits.
Request comments with optional replies and combine multiple video sources in one payload.
Describe synchronous extraction, asynchronous status polling, and dataset retrieval through curl.
Provide Python and JavaScript Apify client examples and describe post and comment output fields.
limitations: The documentation requires a paid Apify account and API token; current provider requirements were not independently verified.
The skill contains instructions only; hosted actor implementations, availability, pricing, and performance were not audited.
Returned data depends on TikTok accessibility and actor behavior; private content access and complete coverage are not established.
The small-result guardrail can misdiagnose billing restrictions. The asynchronous example omits collection limits, polling deadlines, and explicit error handling.

use_cases.title: Compare Brand Activity
use_cases.description: Prepare bounded requests for several public brand profiles, then compare returned views, likes, comments, and posting dates.

use_cases.title: Study Public Conversations
use_cases.description: Request comments and optional replies from selected videos for qualitative review, using approved collection scopes and retention rules.

use_cases.title: Integrate TikTok Extraction
use_cases.description: Adapt the Python or JavaScript client examples to retrieve actor datasets for an existing reporting workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Profile Request
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a request for [public TikTok profile] with at most 20 posts. Identify the actor and prerequisites without running it.

prompt_templates.title: Configure a Filtered Search
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a keyword search for [topic] in [country] during THIS_MONTH, limited to 100 posts. Describe the expected fields and provider dependencies.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: select search filters and output fields.

prompt_templates.title: Collect Comments and Replies
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare requests for comments from [video URLs], with replies enabled and a 50-item limit. Confirm scope and expected charges before any execution.

prompt_templates.title: Design an Asynchronous Integration
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an asynchronous Apify workflow for [approved profiles], capped at 200 collected items. Include secret handling, polling deadlines, bounded retries, and explicit billing-error checks.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: adapt the documented workflow for a controlled integration.

best_practices: Confirm provider terms, approved collection scope, and expected costs before starting paid actor runs.
Keep API tokens outside source files and shared prompts, and use the documented HTTPS authentication flow.
Set collection limits, budgets, and polling deadlines. Diagnose subscription restrictions from explicit provider errors rather than result counts.
anti_patterns: Treating ten or fewer returned items as proof that a paid-plan upgrade is necessary.
Treating dataset retrieval limits as collection budgets or continuing status polling indefinitely.
Claiming verified performance, private-content access, or complete coverage from documentation examples alone.

faq.question: What does this skill provide?
faq.answer: It provides instructions and examples for four Apify actors covering posts, profiles, comments, and location feeds.

faq.question: Does it require an Apify subscription?
faq.answer: The documentation specifies a paid account and API token. Verify current requirements and actor pricing directly with Apify.

faq.question: Which AI tools are listed as supported?
faq.answer: The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code. Execution also requires suitable network access and the selected client tools.

faq.question: Can it collect comments and replies?
faq.answer: The comments actor examples accept video URLs and an includeReplies option, with a maxItems setting for limiting collection.

faq.question: Are the speed and success claims verified?
faq.answer: No. This review examined the skill documentation, not live actor performance, hosted implementations, or TikTok coverage.

faq.question: Does a small result set prove a billing restriction?
faq.answer: No. A small result can be valid. Check explicit provider errors before recommending a subscription change.
